subject: Feature slicing & prorated upgrade path for PulseHealth
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@pulsehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@pulsehealth.com
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Inquiry: flexible upgrade path and proration

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — PulseHealth is excited by the latency profiles and the KV caching behavior. A few procurement/packaging questions came up in our budget sync:

- We expect seats/capacity to grow steadily through Q2 (small pilot -> org-wide). What does your prorated upgrade path look like if we add capacity mid-term?
- Can we enable specific features (advanced observability, canary rollouts, extra retention) only in prod while keeping dev/staging on a smaller tier?
- How do discounts apply if we step down at renewal or downgrade mid-term? Any stepdown penalties or cooling periods?

Could you share a clean set of options (recommended plan, example math for proration, and any constraints around feature-level entitlements)? If helpful, we can schedule a 30m to walk through.

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Singh
Director of Platform
PulseHealth
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Inquiry: flexible upgrade path and proration

Hi Tara — really appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then a proposed set of options below. Attaching a short proposal and a feature matrix for clarity.

TL;DR
- Proration: We prorate capacity purchases on a daily basis. If you add seats mid-term we bill the remainder of the billing period at the committed price; credits can be applied against future invoices for partial-month downgrades.
- Feature entitlements: Yes, we support entitlements per environment (prod/dev/staging) so you can enable advanced observability and longer retention only in prod.
- Stepdowns/downgrades: No punitive early-termination for downgrades, but deep discounts tied to annual commitments have minimum terms — stepping down inside a committed year will convert the outstanding committed dollars into a standard usage billing for the remainder of the term unless we agree to a one-time credit.

Options (recommended):
1) Committed+Burst (recommended for predictable growth)
   - Annual commitment sized to expected Q2 average (e.g., 80 GPUs equivalent), with burst pool for spikes.
   - Mid-term adds are prorated; adds count toward committed total.
   - Downgrades inside the year: we can offer a one-time protection credit of up to 15% of the committed shortfall if you provide a 30-day notice and we re-sell capacity within 60 days.

2) Quarterly Flexible (lower commitment, faster elasticity)
   - Quarterly commit, simpler proration, smaller block discounts.
   - Good for pilot -> small-scale rollouts.

Feature-slicing: We’ll gate observability/retention features via entitlements. That’s a configuration change and does not require separate SKUs — we bill by enabled feature+capacity.

I attached: PulseHealth_PRICING_PROPOSAL_v3.pdf (proposal with line item math) and feature_matrix.xlsx (entitlement mapping by environment).

If you want, we can run two concrete math examples in the doc: (A) add 20% capacity on March 15th on top of an annual commit, (B) step down 30% Dec 1 inside the committed year. Which would you prefer?

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: PulseHealth (PH-482) — approval for 15% one-time protection credit & prod-only entitlements

Karthik / Marcus — looping you both for approval before I respond to Tara with concrete numbers. Context: PulseHealth is leaning toward a large annual commit but wants reassurance around mid-term downgrades. I recommended the 15% protection credit (one-time) conditioned on 30-day notice and Redwood having 60 days to re-sell capacity.

Proposed concession structure:
- One-time protection credit = min(15% of committed shortfall, $60k)
- Applies only if PulseHealth downgrades >20% inside year and provides 30-day notice.
- Standard prorated adds; no change.

Also: they will enable advanced observability only in prod — entitlement gating is straightforward; no extra license needed beyond the feature flag, but we should confirm retention window (we can offer 90 days for prod at +15% charge or 30 days included).

Related: HubSpot deal PH-482 — https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/PH-482. If you approve, I’ll send the worked example and finalize DocuSign.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Hi Tara — thanks for the patience. Per internal approval we can confirm the 15% one-time protection credit under the conditions below. Attached is the updated proposal with worked example (PulseHealth_PRICING_PROPOSAL_v3.pdf). Quick answers:

Worked example (A) — add 20% on March 15th to an annual commit of 80 GPU-equivalents:
- Remaining days in billing year: 291 (Mar 15 -> Dec 31)
- 20% of 80 = 16 GPU-eq. Prorated charge = (16 / 365) * 291 * committed rate = $X (see attached spreadsheet for line math)
- Added capacity counts toward the committed total for the remainder of the term.

Prod-only observability: available via entitlement flag. No additional seat minimum. Retention options: 30 days (included) or 90 days (+15% on observability line).

One-time protection credit: approved at 15% of the committed shortfall, capped at $60k, requires 30-day notice and Redwood has 60 days to re-sell the freed capacity. This is a one-time concession for PH-482 and will be included in the SOW.

Next steps:
